advances:
The declared rational pentagon system is infeasible.  More strongly, the
same conclusion holds for every convex polygon with the stated support edge
and coordinate sign pattern.  An area-preserving support-coordinate change
turns the polygon into the region below a concave function.  The two exact
endpoint caps determine two supporting lines whose tent has area
\[
\frac{s(\delta+a+b)^2}{8a^2+5b^2+2s}.
\]
The prescribed total area forces \(\delta>a+b\), contradicting the
registered strict support order.  Thus the obstruction covers the entire
pentagon cell and is not an area-only relaxation.
author: r097_phase_pentagon
proof:
Apply the affine map
\[
\Phi(x,y)=(\xi,h)=(x+a,\delta-x-y).
\tag{4}
\]
Its linear part has determinant \(-1\), so it preserves area and reverses
orientation.  Put \(\widetilde P=\Phi(P)\).  The first two vertices become
\[
q_0=(0,0),\qquad q_1=(L,0).
\tag{5}
\]
For \(i=2,3,4\), write \(q_i=(\xi_i,h_i)\).  The strict sign hypotheses give
\[
\xi_i>a,\qquad h_i>0,\qquad
\xi_i+h_i=L-b-y(p_i)<L-b.
\tag{6}
\]
In particular, \(0<\xi_i<L\).  Thus \(q_0q_1\) is the bottom edge of
\(\widetilde P\), all other vertices lie strictly above it, and the vertical
sections of \(\widetilde P\) have the form
\[
\widetilde P\cap\{\xi=\tau\}
=\{(\tau,h):0\le h\le f(\tau)\},
\qquad 0\le\tau\le L,
\tag{7}
\]
for a nonnegative concave piecewise-affine function \(f\) satisfying
\[
f(0)=f(L)=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Concavity follows directly from the convexity of \(\widetilde P\).

Write
\[
q_4=(E,v),\qquad q_2=(C,u).
\tag{9}
\]
By (6), \(E>a\), \(v>0\), \(C<L\), and \(u>0\).  The two endpoint edges of
the upper boundary therefore give
\[
f(\tau)=\alpha\tau\quad(0\le\tau\le E),
\qquad
f(\tau)=\beta(L-\tau)\quad(C\le\tau\le L),
\tag{10}
\]
where
\[
\alpha=\frac vE>0,\qquad
\beta=\frac{u}{L-C}>0.
\tag{11}
\]

The line \(x=0\) becomes \(\xi=a\).  Since \(E>a\), the first cap in (1)
is exactly the triangle below the first line in (10), so
\[
\frac{\alpha a^2}{2}=\frac{s}{8},
\qquad
\alpha=\frac{s}{4a^2}.
\tag{12}
\]

The inverse of (4) gives
\[
y=L-b-\xi-h.
\tag{13}
\]
Hence \(y=0\) becomes \(h=L-b-\xi\).  On the right endpoint edge, put
\(r=L-\xi\), so that its upper boundary is \(h=\beta r\), while the
line \(y=0\) is \(h=r-b\).  Since \(p_2\) has positive \(y\), the two
lines meet in the relative interior of \(q_1q_2\), and \(0<\beta<1\).
Their intersection has
\[
r=\frac{b}{1-\beta},
\qquad
h=\frac{b\beta}{1-\beta}.
\tag{14}
\]
The second cap in (1) is therefore the triangle with base \(b\) on
\(q_0q_1\) and the height in (14).  Its exact area equation is
\[
\frac{b^2\beta}{2(1-\beta)}=\frac{s}{5},
\qquad
\beta=\frac{2s}{5b^2+2s}.
\tag{15}
\]

Concavity now bounds the whole upper boundary, not only the two endpoint
edges.  For \(E<\tau\le L\), concavity between \(0\) and \(\tau\) gives
\[
f(E)\ge \frac{E}{\tau}f(\tau),
\]
so \(f(\tau)\le\alpha\tau\).  Equality already holds for
\(0\le\tau\le E\).  Applying the same argument to the concave function
\(r\mapsto f(L-r)\) at the right endpoint gives
\[
f(\tau)\le\beta(L-\tau).
\]
Therefore
\[
f(\tau)\le
\min\{\alpha\tau,\beta(L-\tau)\}
\qquad(0\le\tau\le L).
\tag{16}
\]
The two lines in (16) meet at
\(\tau=\beta L/(\alpha+\beta)\).  Integrating their tent and using
(12) and (15) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
|P|
&=|\widetilde P|
=\int_0^L f(\tau)\,d\tau\\
&\le
\int_0^L\min\{\alpha\tau,\beta(L-\tau)\}\,d\tau\\
&=\frac{\alpha\beta L^2}{2(\alpha+\beta)}
=\frac{L^2}{2(\alpha^{-1}+\beta^{-1})}\\
&=\frac{sL^2}{8a^2+5b^2+2s}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
\]
This proves (2).

If \(|P|=16s\), equation (17) and positivity of its denominator give
\[
L^2\ge16(8a^2+5b^2+2s)
=128a^2+80b^2+32s.
\tag{18}
\]
The lower bound in (18) is strictly larger than \(4(a+b)^2\), because
\[
\begin{aligned}
&128a^2+80b^2+32s-4(a+b)^2\\
&\qquad=120a^2+72b^2+4(a-b)^2+32s>0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{19}
\]
Since \(L,a,b>0\), equations (18)-(19) imply
\[
L>2(a+b).
\]
Finally, \(L=\delta+a+b\), so
\[
\delta=L-a-b>a+b.
\tag{20}
\]
This proves (3) and contradicts the required inequality
\(\delta<a+b\).  The proof used only convexity and the declared strict
signs, so it covers every strictly convex rational pentagon in the sign
cell.
statement:
Let \(s,a,b,\delta>0\), and let \(P\) be a convex pentagon with clockwise
vertices
\[
p_0=(-a,\delta+a),\qquad
p_1=(\delta+b,-b),\qquad
p_2,p_3,p_4.
\]
Assume \(p_2,p_3,p_4\) have positive coordinates and lie strictly below
\(x+y=\delta\), and assume the displayed cyclic order makes \(p_0p_1\) a
support edge.  If
\[
|P\cap\{x\le0\}|=\frac{s}{8},
\qquad
|P\cap\{y\le0\}|=\frac{s}{5},
\tag{1}
\]
then, with \(L=\delta+a+b\),
\[
|P|\le \frac{sL^2}{8a^2+5b^2+2s}.
\tag{2}
\]
Consequently,
\[
|P|=16s
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
\delta>a+b.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, no strictly convex rational pentagon in the declared sign
cell satisfies all four equations and inequalities in the registered
subgoal.
